mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS 3-month moving average (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as a structural improvement that boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses below 96,000 and remains below for 2 months
failure_condition: A 20-day forward return regression shows no statistically significant positive effect of PAYEMS below 96,000 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side expansion, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from baseline when HOUST-INDPRO divergence is present (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 101.5 for three months suggests supply chain normalization, which typically precedes equity market optimism and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than average during INDPRO > 101.5 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of the CPIAUCSL exceeds 273.0 by more than 0.5%, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that prompt S&P 500 forward returns to turn negative over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative when CPIAUCSL 3mo MA > 273.5 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a labor market tightening that increases the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with UNRATE < 4.5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (implied by HOUST) alongside a decline in manufacturing (INDPRO) create a demand-led momentum that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when demand proxies rise and supply indicators fall (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In regimes where GDP growth is missing from the evidence snapshot, the interaction between a rising FEDFUNDS rate and a declining CPIAUCSL inflation rate predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising while CPIAUCSL falling for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the specified FEDFUNDS-CPIAUCSL pattern is present (p > 0.05).
